subject: Model with exogenous composite, two common factors, and categorical indicators

messages.author: 77b34ca104eb12cc
messages.subject: Model with exogenous composite, two common factors, and categorical indicators
parts:
Dear community,

I have a problem and hopefully one more experienced user can help me.
I do a simualtion study for the following model:
model='
             # path model
             ETA1~ XI
             ETA2~ XI + ETA1
            
             # measurement model of common factors
             ETA1=~y1 + y2 + y3
             ETA2=~y4 + y5 + y6
             # composite
             XI<~0.3*x1 + x2 + x3 '

If I use the population correlationmatrix I will get the population parameters. I use the following commands:
test=sem(sample.cov=Sigma, model=model.lavaan, sample.nobs=500)
standardizedSolution(test)
 
But as soon as I categorize all indicators and declare them as ordered, the path from xi to eta1 is underestimated in average:
matrix.ordered =lapply(datkatl,sem,model=model, ordered=c( "x1", "x2" ,"x3" ,"y1" ,"y2" ,"y3" ,"y4", "y5" ,"y6"))
where datkatl is a list containing the samples of the categorical indicators for the Monte Carlo simulation.

Do you have any ideas why this is the case?

Thanks for help and for taking you time!

Best regards,
Florian
